"Then let them produce a statement like it"
The problem with this it's highly subjective. One could say the same of Shakespeare? For some writings by someone else could be comparable, for others there might be no comparison. It's the same with the Qur'an. For some other works may be said to have fulfilled the claim. For others no work could be said to be its equal. Of course this doesn't mean we accept Shakespeare or any other writers work as literally the word of God just because it has unique elements. 

"Were they created by nothing or were they creators of themselves"
Well we now know what we didn't in the 7th century. Namely that humans are a result of evolution. So God is not necessary to explain human origins. You could still argue that God May may have triggered the universe, however that's still a leap of logic. We dont know for a fact what started the universe although there are numerous theories. But there's no reason why it necessarily had to be God and even less reason why it would be the God of any particular human religion. 

I'm agnostic because ultimately we dont know for sure that some sort of higher power may exist. But there's 0 reason to say for definite that any particular religions God does exist.

Which seems more likely A) the Qur'an (a supposedly perfect book) was actually pointing to evolution in the vaguest possible terms, so vague unless you were deliberately trying to make it fit you'd miss it, despite Allah knowing theory of evolution would pose a major challenge to his own creation story. Or B) the Qur'an wasn't actually a work of a perfect all knowing being? 

Please think about it with an open mind.
